To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the UNC-45 protein has a novel inhibitory function in vivo and that the Hsp90 chaperone inhibits the myosin chaperone UNC-45 in vitro.
the myosins-binding domain of the UNC45 chaperone alone is sufficient to function in vivo and that the general chaperones Hsp90 and Hsp70 compete with each other for UNC45 binding.
the myosins of C. elegans are chaperoned by the UCS domain of UNC45 and that the TPR domain of this chaperone inhibits the chaperone action of the UCS domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of UNC-45 in muscle development, and we show that it is the myosin-interacting UCS domain that is essential for UNC-45 activity in vivo.
the role of the Hsp family of molecular chapers in the assembly and function of muscle proteins.
the mechanism of UNC-45 function and the role of Hsp90 in muscle assembly and development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UCS domain of UNC45 is essential for function, but the TPR domain is not.
UCS is the minimal functional unit of UNC-45, and that Hsp90 inhibits UNC-45 action in C. elegan s muscle.
UNC-45 chimeric constructs containing only the UCS domain are able to functionally replace the full-length UNC- 45 protein in Caenorhabdits elegans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UNC-45 acts in a myosin-dependent manner and that Hsp90 is required to regulate UNC-45 function in muscle development and myosin assembly.
the UCS domain, and not the TPR domain, of UNC-45 is essential for myosin binding, and that the UCS domain alone is sufficient to support muscle development and A-band formation in vivo.
the UCS domain of UNC45 is essential for its function, and that the TPR domain is an inhibitory domain, which is relieved by Hsp90.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the myosins and UNC-45 are a chaperoning system that can be uncoupled by the presence of a competing chaperone, Hsp90.
the myosim-binding UCS domain of the UNC45 chaperone can function alone in vivo in C. elegan to promote myosin assembly and that the Hsp90 binding TPR domain is inhibitory to UNC45 function.
UNC-45 has a direct and specific role in the assembly of the myosin thick filament, and that this function is independent of its association with Hsp90.
